value.body: Background verification executives check whether what a job candidate has declared is true: degrees, past jobs, addresses and court records. Screening companies and the HR or risk teams of large employers hire them. A day involves calls and emails to universities and employers, document checks and report writing.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Any graduate; forensic science and law graduates are common

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Case management systems, verification databases, email and phone

items.label: Hires with a flagged discrepancy
items.note: One screening firm's own data: ~4.3% for white-collar and ~5.6% for gig hires; not an industry-wide figure
items.source: AuthBridge Workforce Fraud Files, H1 FY26 (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join screening firms through regular hiring and are trained on verification processes. Attention to detail and spotting forged or altered documents are valued; consent and data-protection rules govern what can be checked.

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is volume-based with turnaround targets.
Next steps: quality analyst, team lead, or fraud and investigation roles.
Overlaps with claims investigation and compliance work.
